reference.title: Single Leg Hip Thrust
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Hips, equipment Body weight, exercise type Strength

breathing.pattern: Exhale as you drive the hips up, inhale as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s up, 0.8 s squeeze, 2 s down

prescription.progression: Pause at the top, then a dumbbell on the hip, then a barbell hip thrust

cues.text: Shoulder blades on the bench edge, arms spread on the bench, right foot flat, left knee lifted.
Breathe out and drive through the right heel to lift the hips.
Hips level with the shoulders, shin vertical, chin tucked. Squeeze the glute.
Breathe in and lower the hips toward the floor under control, pelvis level.
Stay on the bench and repeat; then switch legs.

mistakes.mistake: Arching the low back to get higher
mistakes.fix: Stop when the trunk is level; keep the ribs down and the chin tucked.

mistakes.mistake: Pelvis dropping toward the free leg
mistakes.fix: Keep the hips level; brace and shorten the range if needed.

mistakes.mistake: Foot too far out (hamstrings cramp) or too close (knee strain)
mistakes.fix: Place the foot so the shin is vertical at the top.
Pivot on the shoulder blades; the bench edge stays under the same spot.

kinematics.norm: Knee height bench, about 40-45 cm (common setup; clinical opinion)
Hip reaches neutral at the top, trunk level with the floor (clinical opinion)
About 90 degrees at the top (shin vertical); single-leg bridges at 90 degrees load the hamstrings more than at 135 degrees (Lehecka 2017)
Level at the top; the trunk pivots on the shoulder blades (clinical opinion)
About 1 s up, a short pause, about 2 s down (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #207112, Single Leg Hip Thrust, video (movement reference)
Contreras et al. 2015, gluteus maximus, biceps femoris and vastus lateralis EMG in the back squat and barbell hip thrust (J Appl Biomech 31(6))
Macadam and Feser 2019, gluteus maximus EMG excitation during dynamic body-weight hip extension: a systematic review (Int J Sports Phys Ther 14(1):14-31; PMC6350668)
Lehecka et al. 2017, building a better gluteal bridge: EMG of hip muscles during modified single-leg bridges (Int J Sports Phys Ther 12(4):543-549; PMC5534144)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or cramping occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Make sure the bench cannot slide; set it against a wall.
modify: Low back discomfort: lift less high and brace first.
Hard to keep the pelvis level: use both feet.
regressions: Two-leg hip thrust on the bench.

muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Working-leg hip extensor. The barbell hip thrust gave about twice the mean gluteus maximus activity of the back squat (Contreras 2015), and single-leg versions generally excited the gluteus maximus more than two-leg versions (Macadam 2019).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Assist hip extension; the knee at about 90 degrees keeps them working hard (Lehecka 2017 measured biceps femoris near 75% MVIC in a single-leg bridge at 90 degrees).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Adductor magnus assists hip extension and steadies the thigh (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the pelvis level on the narrow one-foot base.
muscleNotes.quads_r: Hold the knee angle and press the foot into the floor (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Resist the pelvis rotating toward the free leg.
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Resist the pelvis rotating toward the free leg.
muscleNotes.core: Holds the ribs down so the lift comes from the hip, not the low back.
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_l: Hold the free knee up (clinical opinion).
